In [[financial mathematics]], the '''Carr–Madan formula''' of Peter Carr and Dilip B. Madan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dilip B. Madan {{!}} Maryland Smith |url=https://www.rhsmith.umd.edu/directory/dilip-b-madan |access-date=2023-07-30 |website=www.rhsmith.umd.edu}}</ref> shows that the [[analytical solution]] of the [[European option|European]] [[option price]] can be obtained once the explicit form of the [[Characteristic function (probability theory)|characteristic function]] of <math>\log S_T</math>, where <math>S_T</math> is the price of the underlying asset at maturity time <math>T</math>, is available.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Carr|first1=Peter|last2=Madan|first2=Dilip B.|date=1999|title=Option valuation using the fast Fourier transform|journal=Journal of Computational Finance|volume=2|issue=4|pages=61–73|doi=10.21314/JCF.1999.043|citeseerx=10.1.1.348.4044}}</ref> This analytical solution is in the form of the [[Fourier transform]], which then allows for the [[fast Fourier transform]] to be employed to numerically compute option values and [[Greeks (finance)|Greeks]] in an efficient manner.
